medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C and overall cardiovascular risk in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: CG181/PH46: statin indicated for patients with QRISK ≥10% or metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 2.5 mg PO once daily, titrate to 5 mg over 4‑6 weeks as tolerated
medications.purpose: First‑line antihypertensive to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NG136: ACE‑I is recommended first‑line for hypertension in metabolic syndrome

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to 1000 mg BID (max 2 g/day)
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NG28: Metformin is first‑line for pre‑diabetes/high‑risk individuals

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly, increase to 1 mg after 4 weeks (may titrate to 2.4 mg if needed)
medications.purpose: Weight management in obesity (BMI ≥30) with cardiometabolic risk

medications.purpose: Continue current CCB component of antihypertensive regimen
medications.nice_justification: NG136: CCB acceptable as part of combination therapy for hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — BP and metabolic review annually
medications.purpose: Adjunct thiazide diuretic for hypertension control
medications.nice_justification: NG136: Thiazide diuretic can be used as adjunct in hypertension

medications.dose: 50 mg PO every 6‑8 hours PRN for pain

medications.nice_justification: Symptom control not covered by metabolic‑syndrome guideline but required for patient comfort

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential additive effect on serum potassium and renal function; monitor electrolytes and creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and creatinine 1‑2 weeks after starting ramipril and after any dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine may increase rosuvastatin exposure modestly (≈1.3‑1.5×)
interactions_checked.action: Use rosuvastatin 10 mg (not >20 mg) and monitor for myopathy; consider pravastatin if concern

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, consider a DPP‑4 inhibitor such as sitagliptin

Baseline liver function tests not provided – required before starting rosuvastatin; order LFTs.
QRISK 10‑year cardiovascular risk not calculated – needed to confirm statin indication; assume ≥10 % based on risk factors.

Iron studies pending for anemia – defer iron supplementation until aetiology is identified.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses metabolic‑syndrome dyslipidaemia, hypertension, pre‑diabetes and obesity. A moderate‑intensity statin (rosuvastatin 10 mg) is started per CG181/PH46, ramipril is added and titrated per NG136 for blood‑pressure control, metformin MR is introduced for glucose regulation per NG28, and semaglutide is offered for weight loss. Existing antihypertensives (amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide) are continued, and tramadol is maintained for pain. Interactions have been reviewed, renal and liver function tests ordered, and monitoring intervals defined.
